audit_findings.title: Waqoo is in the equity claim but absent from the earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Waqoo reported $4.515 million of external revenue and $3.756 million of segment operating income for January–March 2026; 54.3% of that operating income is approximately $2.040 million, or 4.9% of the $41.5 million anchor, for one quarter; owner earnings impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The operating DCF grows FY2025 owner earnings that contain no Waqoo operations, while the latest balance-sheet bridge includes consolidated Waqoo assets and liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: Because we acquired control of Waqoo, Inc. ("Waqoo") on December 19, 2025 and consolidated the financial information of Waqoo and its subsidiary on a three-month reporting lag, Waqoo’s results of operations did not impact our consolidated results for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter description is demonstrably wrong: FY2025 contains no Waqoo operating results, not a partial year. The first reported quarter shows a contribution large enough to matter, but operating income is not owner earnings and the record does not isolate Waqoo taxes, maintenance capital expenditure, working-capital needs, or minority allocation. The omission could therefore materially raise or lower the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the anchor using Waqoo’s January–March 2026 segment statements and cash-flow detail, calculate Waqoo owner earnings, include only SBC’s economic share, and rerun all scenarios without annualizing an unverified quarter.

audit_findings.title: Core earnings depend on non-arm’s-length related-party customers
audit_findings.magnitude: Related-party revenue was $158.861 million, or 91.5% of $173.607 million FY2025 revenue, and $81.687 million, or 88.6% of $92.249 million revenue, for the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer concentration and controller-influenced fee setting affect the durability of the owner-earnings anchor and the growth and terminal-value assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: Transactions involving related parties cannot be presumed to be carried out on an arm’s-length basis, as the requisite conditions of competitive, free market dealings may not exist.
audit_findings.explanation: No improper pricing or future termination is demonstrated, but nearly all revenue depends on related parties whose transactions cannot be presumed arm’s length. The one-year renewal structure, fee revisions, and controlling-family influence make this reasonably capable of changing sustainable owner earnings. Because approximately half of base operating value is terminal value, an unsupported assumption of durable fees can materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain executed current agreements, fee schedules, renewal and termination correspondence, independent-committee approvals, collection records, and MC financial-capacity evidence; then stress-test owner earnings for arm’s-length repricing, non-renewal, and collection deterioration.

audit_findings.title: Waqoo minority shareholders are an omitted senior economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed noncontrolling interests were $16.079 million; a full deduction equals approximately $0.140 per diluted share, reducing base value from $7.01 to about $6.87 and the 30%-MOS threshold from $4.91 to about $4.81, still approximately $0.69 above the $4.12 price
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash and investments, while minority shareholders own part of the subsidiaries supporting those assets; future consolidated owner earnings also require minority allocation.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, Waqoo remains listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and has minority shareholders whose interests may differ from ours.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted minority claim is a demonstrated bridge defect, although the precise adjustment should match the proportion of consolidated non-operating assets and earnings included elsewhere. Even the conservative full $16.079 million deduction does not change the supplied buy-below conclusion, so it is not material at the current valuation margin.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 NCI by subsidiary to cash, investments, debt, and operating earnings; deduct the applicable minority claim or use proportionate assets and owner earnings in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: A contractual $5 million investment obligation is missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.000 million, equal to approximately $0.043 per diluted share and $0.030 per share after the 30% margin of safety; a full deduction would lower buy-below from $4.91 to about $4.88, still above the $4.12 price
audit_findings.mechanism: The commitment reduces future available cash, while the newly purchased OT Midco units may create an offsetting investment asset in stakes_net.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we committed to subscribe for and purchase additional common units in December 2026 for an aggregate purchase price of $5.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q confirms that the obligation remains outstanding and is not recorded as a liability. Its gross amount is only 0.6% of the $806 million base equity value and cannot change the current conclusion even if deducted with no value assigned to the additional units. The net direction remains mixed because the payment purchases incremental ownership rather than representing a pure expense.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the commitment was paid, amended, or cancelled after June 2026 and determine the value and ownership percentage of the units received; update cash and stakes_net together.

audit_findings.title: A second partial-year acquisition was omitted from the perimeter analysis
audit_findings.magnitude: MB career lounge cost $14.150 million plus $0.975 million of transaction costs and produced a $22.598 million acquired service-agreement asset; disclosed revenue from the two named related-party customers was $0.403 million in FY2025 and $0.420 million in the first six months of 2026; standalone owner earnings are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Only post-July 17, 2025 MB results enter the $41.5 million anchor, so applying consolidated growth without a like-for-like adjustment may omit earnings or losses from the unrecorded portion of the year.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 17, 2025, the Company acquired MB career lounge, a Japan-based management support services provider that provides management and operational support services to “JUN CLINIC,” an aesthetic dermatology and plastic-surgery platform.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted acquisition is a demonstrated perimeter-analysis error. The named-customer revenue is small relative to consolidated revenue, but the filing does not provide MB’s complete standalone revenue, expenses, maintenance investment, or working-capital movements. The record therefore cannot establish whether the incomplete year is material or which direction normalization would move value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain MB’s monthly pre- and post-acquisition income statements, cash flows, and customer-level revenue for 2025–2026; calculate full-year owner earnings and rerun the anchor on a consistent perimeter.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a disclosed one-time tax cost
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed one-time tax expense was $2.813 million, equal to 6.8% of the $41.5 million anchor; if fully retained, proportional scaling of the unchanged base DCF implies approximately $39.5 million or $0.344 per share of additional value and about $0.241 per share after the 30% margin of safety
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax expense retained in owner earnings lowers the anchor and every projected year and terminal value derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase of 1.36 percentage points was mainly due to the deemed contribution in connection with the price modification on disposal of an aircraft (a one-time item) to General Incorporated Association SBC, an entity controlled by the CEO of the Company, who is also the controlling shareholder of the Company, which was treated as a taxable gain under the Japanese tax law with no corresponding income being recognized for consolidation purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the owner-earnings calculation retained the charge is unresolved. Even assuming full retention and full normalization, the correction only increases the supplied buy-below threshold from approximately $4.91 to $5.15; the $4.12 price remains below it. It therefore cannot reverse the valuation conclusion, although it affects the value estimate.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $2.813 million charge through the tax and owner-earnings schedules and review subsequent controller-related transfers; rerun only if the charge is present and evidence supports treating it as nonrecurring economic leakage.
